verified_strengths: Croissant 1.1 and Frictionless v1 local ingestion profiles have extensive file-backed positive, negative, integrity, and normalized-input tests.
The lifecourse integration has normative fixtures for EVPI, EVPPI, EVSI, and ENBS plus a versioned result-envelope schema.
The customer-churn example executes deterministically through public VOI methods.
Enterprise adapter records have a versioned schema and six normative synthetic payload shapes.
All 12 named synthetic analysis families have committed fixture files.

findings.summary: Every registered dataset uses an all-zero placeholder snapshot hash even though seven snapshot files exist.
findings.required_disposition: Bind each registry record to an actual reviewed snapshot digest or explicitly classify the file as synthetic/illustrative and remove the false integrity field.

findings.summary: The dataset documentation advertises refresh_all.py and source-specific transforms, but the transform directory contains only a README.
findings.required_disposition: Implement deterministic, provenance-recording transforms with bounded live-network lanes, or change registry and documentation claims to an explicit fixture-only status.

findings.summary: The legacy ecosystem connector advertises bidirectional TreeAge and R-package formats that are not demonstrated against authoritative exports; .rds is listed but the implementation reads JSON, and the TreeAge tests use repository-invented XML.
findings.required_disposition: Narrow and rename the surfaces to documented interchange profiles unless authoritative fixtures and real-tool round trips can be legally and reproducibly validated.

findings.summary: Six of nine domain templates have no worked example; the three example mappings resolve to only two scripts, and the market-entry script does not exercise the template registry.
findings.required_disposition: Add deterministic registry-driven workflows for accepted domains, prioritizing both stable templates, and label the remainder as templates rather than validated domain integrations.

findings.summary: The repository contains 14 Python examples and 23 notebooks, but no complete example/notebook execution lane; most checks inspect filenames or cell text rather than executing the workflow.
findings.required_disposition: Define a deterministic smoke manifest, execute supported scripts and notebooks in a focused cached lane, and quarantine hardware, interactive, or obsolete examples with explicit reasons.

findings.summary: Six enterprise adapter shapes are schema-tested only with hand-authored payloads; compatibility with versioned MLflow, OpenLineage, dbt, experimentation, CATE, and forecast exports is not demonstrated.
findings.required_disposition: Describe these as SDK-free interchange constructors and add redacted, version-pinned producer fixtures before claiming product compatibility.

findings.summary: There is no manifest proving realistic source-to-ingestion-to-analysis-to-serialized-result-to-report execution across the claimed health, environmental, financial, and enterprise domains.
findings.required_disposition: Create a small rights-cleared workflow corpus with provenance, expected numerical results, serialized contracts, and report assertions for each accepted representative domain.

findings.summary: The data-format connector advertises Excel import/export, but openpyxl is absent from package extras and the two focused Excel tests skip in the standard development environment.
findings.required_disposition: Add an explicit Excel extra and required CI lane, or remove Excel from advertised built-in formats and fail with a targeted optional-dependency diagnostic.

boundary: This audit is repository evidence only. It does not assert compatibility with proprietary products, validate remote source rights, or promote an experimental domain or adapter.
